questions.solution:
Let the given expression be $\alpha$. First, we simplify the angles in the product.

$\cos\left(\dfrac{27\pi}{11}\right) = \cos\left(2\pi + \dfrac{5\pi}{11}\right) = \cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{11}\right)$

$\cos\left(\dfrac{81\pi}{11}\right) = \cos\left(7\pi + \dfrac{4\pi}{11}\right) = -\cos\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{11}\right) = \cos\left(\pi - \dfrac{4\pi}{11}\right) = \cos\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{11}\right)$

Thus, the angles are $\dfrac{\pi}{11}, \dfrac{3\pi}{11}, \dfrac{5\pi}{11}, \dfrac{7\pi}{11}, \dfrac{9\pi}{11}$, which can be written as $\theta_k = \dfrac{(2k-1)\pi}{11}$ for $k = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5$.

The expression becomes:
$\alpha = \prod_{k=1}^{5} \left(1 - 2\cos\theta_k\right)$

Using the trigonometric identity $1 - 2\cos\theta = 1 - 2(2\cos^2(\theta/2) - 1) = 3 - 4\cos^2(\theta/2)$.
Multiplying and dividing by $\cos(\theta/2)$, we get:
$1 - 2\cos\theta = \dfrac{3\cos(\theta/2) - 4\cos^3(\theta/2)}{\cos(\theta/2)} = -\dfrac{\cos(3\theta/2)}{\cos(\theta/2)}$

Applying this identity to the product:
$\alpha = \prod_{k=1}^{5} \left( -\dfrac{\cos(3\theta_k/2)}{\cos(\theta_k/2)} \right) = (-1)^5 \dfrac{\prod_{k=1}^{5} \cos(3\theta_k/2)}{\prod_{k=1}^{5} \cos(\theta_k/2)}$

The terms in the denominator are $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{22}\right), \cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{22}\right), \cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{22}\right), \cos\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{22}\right), \cos\left(\dfrac{9\pi}{22}\right)$.

The terms in the numerator are $\cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{22}\right), \cos\left(\dfrac{9\pi}{22}\right), \cos\left(\dfrac{15\pi}{22}\right), \cos\left(\dfrac{21\pi}{22}\right), \cos\left(\dfrac{27\pi}{22}\right)$.

We can simplify the larger angles in the numerator:
$\cos\left(\dfrac{15\pi}{22}\right) = \cos\left(\pi - \dfrac{7\pi}{22}\right) = -\cos\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{22}\right)$

$\cos\left(\dfrac{21\pi}{22}\right) = \cos\left(\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{22}\right) = -\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{22}\right)$

$\cos\left(\dfrac{27\pi}{22}\right) = \cos\left(\pi + \dfrac{5\pi}{22}\right) = -\cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{22}\right)$

Substituting these back into the numerator product:
$\prod_{k=1}^{5} \cos(3\theta_k/2) = \cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{22}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{9\pi}{22}\right) \left(-\cos\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{22}\right)\right) \left(-\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{22}\right)\right) \left(-\cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{22}\right)\right)$

$\prod_{k=1}^{5} \cos(3\theta_k/2) = - \left[ \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{22}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{22}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{22}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{22}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{9\pi}{22}\right) \right]$

Notice that the term in the brackets is exactly the denominator product. Therefore, the ratio of the numerator product to the denominator product is $-1$.

$\alpha = (-1)^5 \times (-1) = (-1) \times (-1) = 1$

We need to find the value of $5 - \alpha^2$:
$5 - (1)^2 = 5 - 1 = 4$

Answer: $4$

questions.q: Let $\alpha = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{\infty}\sin^{2k}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$. Let $g: \left[0, 1\right] \to \mathbb{R}$ be the function defined by $g\left(x\right) = {2}^{ax} + {2}^{a\left(1 - x\right)}$. Then, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
options: The function $g\left(x\right)$ attains its maximum at more than one point
The function $g\left(x\right)$ attains its minimum at more than one point
questions.solution:
Given,

$\alpha = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{\infty}\sin^{2k}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$ and $g\left(x\right) = {2}^{ax} + {2}^{a\left(1 - x\right)}$.

Now solving,

$\alpha = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{\infty}{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}^{2k} = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{\infty}{\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)}^{k} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{4}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Now putting the value of $\alpha$ in $g\left(x\right)$ we get,

$g\left(x\right) = 2\dfrac{x}{3} + 2\dfrac{\left(1 - x\right)}{3}$

Now, ${g}^{'}\left(x\right) = \dfrac{ln2}{3}\dfrac{\left({2}^{\dfrac{2x}{3}} - {2}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}\right)}{{2}^{\dfrac{x}{3}}}$

Now finding the critical point by ${g}^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$$⇒ x = \dfrac{1}{2}$

And, derivative changes sign from negative to positive at $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, hence $x = \dfrac{1}{2}$ is point of local minimum as well as absolute minimum of $g\left(x\right)$ for $x \in \left[0, 1\right]$

Hence, minimum value of $g\left(x\right) = g\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

$= 2\dfrac{1}{6} + 2\dfrac{1}{6} = 2\dfrac{7}{6}$

$⇒$ Option $\left(A\right)$ is correct

Now maximum value of $g\left(x\right)$ is either equal to $g\left(0\right)$ or $g\left(1\right)$.

$g\left(0\right) = 1 + 2\dfrac{1}{3}$

$g\left(1\right) = 2\dfrac{1}{3} + 1$

Hence (B) and (C) are also correct.

questions.q:
For non-negative integers $n,$ let
$f\left(n\right) = \dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{k + 1}{n + 2}\pi\right)sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{k + 2}{n + 2}\pi\right)}{\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}\sin^{2} ⁡ \left(\dfrac{k + 1}{n + 2}\pi\right)}$
Assuming $\cos^{- 1} ⁡ x$ takes values in $\left[0, \pi\right],$ which of the following options is/are correct?
questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{ll}f\left(n\right) = \dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}sin ⁡ \left(\left(\dfrac{k + 1}{n + 2}\right)\pi\right)sin ⁡ \left(\left(\dfrac{k + 2}{n + 2}\right)\pi\right)}{\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}si{n}^{2}\left(\left(\dfrac{k + 1}{n + 2}\right)\pi\right)}\end{array}$

$\left(\begin{array}{ll}∵ 2sinC ⁡ sin ⁡ D = cos ⁡ \left(C - D\right) - cos ⁡ \left(C + D\right) \\ ∵ 2\sin^{2} ⁡ \theta = 1 - cos ⁡ 2\theta\end{array}\right)$
$f\left(n\right) = \dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}\left(cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}\right) - cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{2k + 3}{n + 2}\pi\right)\right)}{\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}\left(1 - cos ⁡ \left(\left(\dfrac{2k + 2}{n + 2}\right)\pi\right)\right)}$
$f\left(n\right) = \dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}\right) - \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{2k + 3}{n + 2}\right)\pi}{\left(n + 1\right) - \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{n}cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{2k + 2}{n + 2}\right)\pi}$
Now $cos ⁡ \alpha + cos ⁡ \left(\alpha + \beta\right) + \ldots + cos ⁡ \left(\alpha + \left(n - 1\right)\beta\right) = \dfrac{sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{n\beta}{2}\right)}{sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\beta}{2}\right)}cos ⁡ \left(\alpha + \dfrac{\left(n - 1\right)\beta}{2}\right)$
$f\left(n\right) = \dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}\right) - \dfrac{sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{n + 1}{n + 2}\pi\right)}{sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}\right)}cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{n + 3}{n + 2}\pi\right)}{\left(n + 1\right) - \dfrac{sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{n + 1}{n + 2}\right)\pi}{sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}\right)}cos ⁡ \left(\pi\right)}$
In numerator cosine sum $\alpha = \dfrac{3\pi}{n + 2}$
$\beta = \dfrac{2\pi}{n + 2}$
Number of terms $= \left(n + 1\right)$
In denominator cosine sum $\alpha = \dfrac{2\pi}{n + 2}$
$\beta = \dfrac{2\pi}{n + 2}$
Number of terms $= \left(n + 1\right)$
Now $sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{n + 1}{n + 2}\pi\right) = sin ⁡ \left(\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}\right) = sin ⁡ \dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}$
$cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{n + 3}{n + 2}\pi\right) = cos ⁡ \left(\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}\right) = - cos ⁡ \dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}$
$f\left(n\right) = \dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}\right) + cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}\right)}{\left(n + 1\right) - \left(- 1\right)}$
$f\left(n\right) = \dfrac{cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}\right)\left(n + 2\right)}{\left(n + 2\right)}$
$f\left(n\right) = cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{n + 2}\right)$
Hence, $\left(A\right)f\left(4\right) = cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
$\left(B\right)\lim_{n + \infty} ⁡ f\left(n\right) = cos ⁡ \left(0\right) = 1$
$\left(C\right)f\left(6\right) = cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right):$ then $\alpha = tan ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right) = \sqrt{2} - 1$
$\alpha = \sqrt{2}\left(5\right) = cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\pi}{7}\right)$
$sin ⁡ \left(7\cos^{- 1} ⁡ \left(cos ⁡ \dfrac{\pi}{7}\right)\right) = sin ⁡ \pi = 0$

questions.q: The value of ${sec}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(\dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{10}sec ⁡ \left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2}\right)sec ⁡ \left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{\left(k + 1\right)\pi}{2}\right)\right)$ in the interval $\left[- \dfrac{\pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right]$ equals
questions.solution:
${\text{sec}}^{- 1} \left[\dfrac{1}{4} \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{10} sec\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2}\right)sec\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right]$
$\begin{cases}= {\text{sec}}^{- 1} \left[\dfrac{- 1}{4} \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{10} sec\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2}\right)\text{cosec}\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2}\right)\right] & \left(∴ sec\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \theta\right) = - \text{cosec}\theta\right)\end{cases}$
$= {sec}^{- 1}\left(- \dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{10}\dfrac{1}{cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2}\right)sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2}\right)}\right)$
$\begin{cases}= {sec}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(- \dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{10}\dfrac{2}{sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{7\pi}{6} + k\pi\right)}\right) & \left(∴ 2sin ⁡ \thetacos ⁡ \theta = sin ⁡ 2\theta\right)\end{cases}$
now if $\begin{cases}k = even & sin ⁡ \left(2n\pi + \dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right) = sin ⁡ \dfrac{7\pi}{6} = - \dfrac{1}{2}\end{cases}$
and if $\begin{cases}k = odd & sin ⁡ \left(\left(2n + 1\right)\pi + \dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right) = - sin ⁡ \dfrac{7\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\end{cases}$
hence
$= {sec}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{- \dfrac{1}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{- \dfrac{1}{2}} + \ldots . .\right)\right)$
$= {sec}^{- 1} ⁡ 1$
$= 0$

${\text{sec}}^{- 1} \left[\dfrac{1}{4} \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{10} sec\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2}\right)sec\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)\right]$
$\begin{cases}= {\text{sec}}^{- 1} \left[\dfrac{- 1}{4} \mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{10} sec\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2}\right)\text{cosec}\left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2}\right)\right] & \left(∴ sec\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} + \theta\right) = - \text{cosec}\theta\right)\end{cases}$
$= {sec}^{- 1}\left(- \dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{10}\dfrac{1}{cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2}\right)sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{7\pi}{12} + \dfrac{k\pi}{2}\right)}\right)$
$\begin{cases}= {sec}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(- \dfrac{1}{4}\mathop{∑}_{k = 0}^{10}\dfrac{2}{sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{7\pi}{6} + k\pi\right)}\right) & \left(∴ 2sin ⁡ \thetacos ⁡ \theta = sin ⁡ 2\theta\right)\end{cases}$
now if $\begin{cases}k = even & sin ⁡ \left(2n\pi + \dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right) = sin ⁡ \dfrac{7\pi}{6} = - \dfrac{1}{2}\end{cases}$
and if $\begin{cases}k = odd & sin ⁡ \left(\left(2n + 1\right)\pi + \dfrac{7\pi}{6}\right) = - sin ⁡ \dfrac{7\pi}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}\end{cases}$
hence
$= {sec}^{- 1} ⁡ \left(- \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{- \dfrac{1}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{1}{2}} + \dfrac{1}{- \dfrac{1}{2}} + \ldots . .\right)\right)$
$= {sec}^{- 1} ⁡ 1$
$= 0$

questions.q: Let $a, b, c$ be three non-zero real numbers such that the equation $\sqrt{3}acos ⁡ x + 2bsin ⁡ x = c, x \in \left[- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$ has two distinct real roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with $\alpha + \beta = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$. Then, the value of $\dfrac{b}{a}$ is
questions.solution:
$\sqrt{3}cos ⁡ x + \dfrac{2b}{a}sin ⁡ x = \dfrac{c}{a}$
Now, $\sqrt{3}cos ⁡ \alpha + \dfrac{2b}{a}sin ⁡ \alpha = \dfrac{c}{a} \ldots \left(i\right)
$\sqrt{3}cos ⁡ \beta + $\dfrac{2b}{a}$sin ⁡ \beta = $\dfrac{c}{a}$ \ldots $\left(ii\right)$

From equations $\left(i\right)$ and $\left(ii\right)$

$⇒ \sqrt{3}\left[cos ⁡ \alpha - cos ⁡ \beta\right] + \dfrac{2b}{a}\left(sin ⁡ \alpha - sin ⁡ \beta\right) = 0$
$⇒ \sqrt{3}\left[- 2sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\right)sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\alpha - \beta}{2}\right)\right] + \dfrac{2b}{a}\left[2cos ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\alpha + \beta}{2}\right)sin ⁡ \left(\dfrac{\alpha - \beta}{2}\right)\right] = 0$

$⇒ - \sqrt{3} + 2\sqrt{3} \cdot \dfrac{b}{a} = 0$
$⇒ \dfrac{b}{a} = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5$
